description: Runner with active shin splints (can only run 3mi pain-free) wants a 10k in 12 weeks. Plan must use run-walk protocol, conservative build, and treat the injury seriously.

user.name: Keisha
user.experience_level: intermediate — running 2 years, multiple 5k finishes, currently sidelined with shin splints after ramping too fast
user.injury_notes: Active medial shin splints — currently limited to 3 miles per run before pain sets in. Has been running through mild discomfort. Doctor cleared her to run but recommended gradual return and no intensity until pain-free for 2 weeks.
user.notes: Goal is to finish the 10k healthy. Open to run-walk approach. Has been cross-training on the bike during flare-ups.

forbidden_content: running through pain or ignoring the shin splint injury
introducing intensity (tempo, intervals) in the first 3-4 weeks
prescribing daily running with no recovery days
no mention of the injury or conservative return-to-run approach
ground_truth.notes: 12-week return-to-running 10k plan for someone with active shin splints. This is an injury rehab context — the plan MUST acknowledge the injury and build conservatively. Week 1 should be 8-12mi max with individual runs capped at 3-4mi (current pain-free limit). No intensity whatsoever for the first 3-4 weeks while she confirms the shins are healing. Run-walk approach for longer efforts is appropriate. Long run caps at 7-8mi — the race is 6.2mi, she doesn't need 12-mile long runs. Cross-training on rest days (bike, pool) should be mentioned as a bridge. If she starts adding intensity too early she'll re-injure.
